text:
Jordan: FYI — noticed employer match looks low for a few mid‑Jan hires after the vendor switch. Can someone confirm?
PayrollBot: Payroll run 2025-01-31 completed. 4 matches flagged as ‘pending vendor mapping’. See report link: https://vendor.example/reports/flagged
Anya: Which employees? Is this a timing/effective date issue or a plan mapping problem?
Jordan: Looks like hire dates 2025-01-10 through 2025-01-20. Vendor mapped their enrollments to the old plan ID, so match percentage defaulted to 0%. CSV snippet from the vendor report:```employee_id,hire_date,enrolled_plan,match_pct
E1023,2025-01-10,OLD_PLAN,0
E1045,2025-01-14,OLD_PLAN,0
E1056,2025-01-18,OLD_PLAN,0
E1089,2025-01-20,OLD_PLAN,0```
Sam (Benefits): Ugh. Thanks for catching. Per the SOW the switch date should have mapped new hires after 2025-01-12 to NEW_PLAN (4% match). Does Redwood have a vesting schedule on match for these hires?
Luis: Plan doc shows immediate vesting for the employer match (sec 3.2). So we should be able to do a retroactive employer contribution for those pay periods.
Anya: Great. What do we need from payroll/vendor to fix? Manual JE? Corrected contribution file to vendor? Backdated payroll adj?
Sam (Benefits): We'll need the vendor to accept a retro contribution file and payroll to create the manual employer contribution entries. Also we need letter to affected employees explaining the correction and confirming taxable treatment.
Jordan: I can pull the payroll export and populate the retro contribution amounts. Quick calc: each missed match ≈ 4% of deferrals that pay period — I have the deferral amounts in the export.
Anya: Jordan, please share employee IDs + gross/deferral amounts here (or DM if PII). Payroll, can you confirm you can run a retro JE to hit Q1 journal? @PayrollBot any constraints?
PayrollBot: Payroll Ops: retro adjustments allowed before EOY close. Submit Ticket: #payroll-retro with CSV + GL account. Deadline to include in Jan financials: 2025-02-10.
Luis: I'll draft the vendor support request. Does vendor need a signed amendment or just the corrected file? Vendor SLA team should confirm.
Sam (Benefits): Vendor usually accepts corrected contribution batches with a signed attestation for mapping errors. I’ll attach the attestation template. Also we should check IRS limits — none of these are over limits, but call out catch‑up eligibility if any employee is 50+.
Jordan: One of them (E1023) is 51 and had catch‑up elected. That complicates matching math (match only applies to elective deferrals up to limit). I’ll note catch‑up separately in the file.
Anya: Good catch. Make sure retro file has fields: employee_id, retro_match_amount, retro_catchup_flag, plan_id, pay_period. Use this CSV header template.
Jordan: Will do. I’ll DM payroll the PII export and post a redacted summary here when complete.
Sam (Benefits): After vendor confirms, we’ll send the employee notification draft. Also alert finance for GL impact.
Luis: Putting a calendar reminder for the 02/10 deadline + creating vendor ticket now.
Jordan: Quick question for the people-ops channel: should we proactively check Jan new hires cohort for any other mapping issues?
Anya: Yes — please run a small audit for hires 2025-01-01 through 2025-01-31. If there are more than 10 issues escalate to me.
Jordan: On it. Summary update when done. :thumbsup:
Sam (Benefits): Thanks team — once payroll confirms ticket # and vendor ack, I’ll close the loop with employee comms.
Luis: TL;DR: vendor mis-mapped 4 new hires to OLD_PLAN -> match 0% -> fix via retro contribution + payroll JE + employee notice.
Jordan: Update: audit complete, only those 4 affected. DMing details to Payroll.
Anya: Thanks, everyone.
PayrollBot: Ticket #payroll-retro-789 created by @Luis. Status: awaiting CSV upload. Deadline 2025-02-10.
